title: Hugging Face added a pipeline that returns a choice, not a paragraph
friendlyTitle: Hugging Face added a model type that picks an answer instead of writing one
summary: On 10 November, Hugging Face documented decision models in Transformers. You pass a state and one or more questions with allowed answers. The model returns a choice, or a score, and a probability. It does not write the answer token by token. The post's example uses the pipeline name "decision" and the model autotrust/GEV-26B-Decide.
friendlySummary: On 10 November, Hugging Face showed how to use a decision model in its Transformers library. You give it the situation and a list of allowed answers. It returns a choice and a probability. It does not write a paragraph. The example uses a model called autotrust/GEV-26B-Decide.
whyItMatters: This is the same job Amazon's ticket system just moved off a chat model: routing, urgency, and yes-or-no labels. A normal classifier has its labels baked in. A decision model takes the allowed answers at request time, and can ask several typed questions about one state. It is not a replacement for writing, coding, or any answer that is not on the list you supplied.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Use this for sorting, routing, or a yes-or-no label. You can change the allowed answers without retraining a fixed classifier. Do not use it to write, code, or answer a question that is not on your list.
